title: Lightning Safety in the Backcountry — NOLS
claims: In the backcountry, defined as 30 minutes or more from modern vehicles or buildings, there are no safe places from lightning; the 0-10 safety scale rates a modern building or vehicle 10 and nothing in the backcountry above 3.

The lightning position means standing or squatting with feet close together to protect from ground current; more than half of lightning fatalities are caused by ground current as body parts touch the ground far enough apart.

The four major ways to reduce lightning risk are timing visits with local weather patterns, finding safer terrain when hearing thunder, avoiding trees and long conductors once lightning gets close, and taking the lightning position if lightning is striking nearby and safer terrain cannot be reached.
